newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parties still not agreed on holding firms.
newsitem.headline: Japan parties still not agreed on holding firms.

text.p: Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on Monday failed again to reach an agreement with its allies on a plan to lift a decades-long ban on holding companies but aims to do so on Tuesday.

An LDP official quoted Taku Yamasaki, chairman of the LDP's policy-making committee, as saying after a meeting between the LDP, the Social Democratic Party and the small Sakigake Party, that he would finalise a plan to lift the ban on Tuesday and would finish discussions on the issue.
An agreement among the parties would enable the government to make changes to Japan's anti-monopoly law and submit them to the current session of parliament by March 11, he said.
The parties have been trying to reach agreement on the issue since the middle of last week.
Yamasaki said that while they basically agreed on lifting the ban, they have not yet agreed guidelines as to what size of holding companies should be allowed.
He said the parties plan to come a final agreement on Tuesday even though management and the unions have also not agreed on labour issues that may result from the lifting of the ban,
